column1: # The FALCO_CTF_IMAGE_TAG grammar's shared case table (app#510, #507 review-5x R1#1).
# FALCO_CTF_IMAGE_TAG is the one tag the three images (ttyd, ttyd-proxy, challenge)
# are pulled with (I5: the same SHA across all of them; the chart's `*.image.tag`).
# The grammar is the OCI tag: `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}` (1 to 128
# characters, the first not a `.` or `-`). A digest (`sha256:...`) is not a tag and
# The grammar has NO Go definition: the shell literal is the definition. The readers:
#   - Go:    internal/catalog (deploy_operator_inputs_test.go) pins the header to the
#            shell literal, and runs every row.
#   - shell: charts/ctf-user/deploy-user.sh, run row by row as the env
# An empty value has no row: an empty FALCO_CTF_IMAGE_TAG means "not set" (the chart
# default is kept), as it always has.
# Format: the same as internal/identity/testdata/seat-cases.tsv (see its header):
# {U+00EF}, line 1 the canonical `# pattern: ` literal. The table stays ASCII.
# The input is the value as the operator gives it, with the one exception that an
# empty value has no row (see below). A row is never dropped to make an
# implementation pass: the implementation that disagrees is the bug.
# --- baseline: a git SHA, a release tag, the chart default
# --- a value helm would type or delete: valid tags, which is why the value goes in with --set-string
# --- the first character is a letter, a digit or `_`
# --- what a tag is not: a digest, a path, a reference
# --- helm --set syntax: a `,` starts another key, `=` another assignment
# --- line breaks, a bidi control, a non-ASCII letter
